analysis.title: Oil Strategy: Thinking Downstream
key_insights: Global refined product markets remain tight. Gasoline inventories are about 13% below pre-conflict levels, fuel oil down 8% and diesel down 6%, while jet fuel has just recovered above pre-war levels.

Gasoline stocks sit below the 5-year range, while diesel and fuel oil sit just above 5-year minimums. Diesel faces winter heating and commercial demand while gasoline benefits from the end of summer driving season.

RBC forecasts net refinery capacity additions of ~470 kb/d in 2026, ~910 kb/d in 2027 and ~450 kb/d in 2028. Revisions reflect minor ramp delays and a few incremental restarts, and multi-year lead times limit near-term relief.
APAC leads capacity growth, with India adding about 400 kb/d in 2027 and 100 kb/d in 2028. China's new capacity such as Panjin skews to petrochemicals, which limits product relief.
Incremental restarts include Valero's 165 kb/d Houston refinery (closed by LyondellBasell in 2025) and a partial restart of China's Dalian refinery.

Russian refinery attacks returned in force after a brief October hiatus. November utilization is roughly 51% and about 2.6 mb/d is offline from Ukraine-related damage, with possible further upside to the outage number.

The Russia-US diesel deal and Trump's unconfirmed energy ceasefire announcement did not materialize. Russian diesel shipments failed to land in the US on sanctions fears and are going to buyers like Brazil.

Middle East energy infrastructure remains under fire, including East-West pipeline pumping stations, the port of Jizan, and a Houthi claim of a strike on Saudi Arabia's 400 kb/d Rabigh refinery. About 1.7 mb/d is offline, with about 1 mb/d needing several months to repair.

The US, Russia and China are each constrained in boosting product supply. US refiners ran at about 96% in November and 94% over the war, US product exports are up about 400 kb/d y/y, and US diesel inventories are below 5-year lows.

China's Shandong independent refinery margins are around -600 RMB/mt per SCI. Remaining export quota could encourage more exports, but any uplift would skew to gasoline and jet rather than diesel and follows China's domestic priorities.
RBC sees refinery margins staying elevated into winter, with normalization a 2027 story at the earliest and contingent on conflict resolution and repair timelines.

market_movers.rationale: Valero plans to restart the 165 kb/d Houston refinery, which LyondellBasell closed in 2025. It is cited as an incremental capacity restart.

sector_views.rationale: RBC expects refinery margins to remain elevated on constrained supply and tight diesel into winter, with normalization in 2027 at the earliest.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Initial November data show weak Russian runs, which limits product exports and supports global margins.
RBC damage-tracking estimate, with risk of further upside as attacks persist.
About 1 mb/d requires several months to repair, delaying margin normalization.
Additions are modest and skewed to petrochemicals in China, so product relief is limited.
US refiners have little room to add output, so diesel remains tight.

risk_factors: Resolution or ceasefire in the Russia-Ukraine or Middle East conflicts could ease product tightness faster than RBC expects.
Chinese refiners may lean into exports using remaining quota.
Capacity additions could face revision and delay, including the Dangote expansion.
Gasoline demand relief has already weighed on refinery margins.
High US diesel-driven run rates could pressure gasoline.

Figure 3 shows estimated quarterly refinery capacity additions by region through 4Q28 with annual net adds of about 474, 913 and 451 kb/d per Appendix 1.
geopolitical: Russia-Ukraine: Ukraine's refinery strikes continue and a Trump-announced energy ceasefire was unconfirmed and did not materialize.
US-Iran conflict and Middle East: negotiations remain fraught with unresolved dealbreakers and signs of escalation.
Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery, and there were attacks on the port of Jizan and East-West pipeline pumping stations.
Sanctions complications hinder Russian refinery repairs and Russia-US diesel shipments.

tension_points.bull_case: Restarts such as Houston and Dalian, available Chinese export quota, and gasoline seasonal relief could ease product tightness.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC argues Russian and Middle East damage, multi-year capacity lead times, and tight diesel into winter keep margins elevated with normalization a 2027 story at the earliest.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material shift in the conflict landscape or a halt to Ukrainian refinery strikes would invalidate the view that margins stay elevated.

theme_stances.key_argument: Conflict-driven outages and slow capacity additions keep refinery margins elevated with diesel tight into winter.
theme_stances.evidence: we see margins remaining elevated and the path to normalization as a 2027 story
